verdict.root_cause: Every complete checkout trace fails at the same edge: checkoutservice's call to ShippingService/GetQuote returns ERROR, propagating up through PlaceOrder to the frontend HTTP POST (tr_89474c9be033). The failing spans are sub-millisecond to a few milliseconds and whole failing requests finish under ~17ms, so this is a fast rejection, not a wait. All sibling dependencies in those same traces (cartservice, productcatalogservice, featureflagservice, currencyservice) are present, fast and unflagged, and checkout never reaches payment, email or the message-bus write — which explains the initiation-only log pattern after ~12:54 (tr_dc4dd324c0ed) and emailservice's flat-zero error ratio (tr_c0d43c9cb03d); the 12:56:15 alert fan-out is downstream starvation, not independent failure. The failing mechanism sits inside shippingservice or its own quote dependency (quoteservice alerted at 12:56:15), but no dispatch touched either service in any modality, so the mechanism itself — wrong artifact, wrong config value, or immediate rejection under resource exhaustion — is unidentified. The two change queries that ran cover only checkoutservice and paymentservice and only from 12:43 (tr_8361564246d9, tr_d2099c6952f8).
verdict.reasoning: Localization is strong, classification is not. The traces put one erroring span on every failing path while showing sibling dependencies healthy in the same traces (tr_89474c9be033); logs corroborate from the other side, with orders initiating through 12:57:52, no error lines, and no completion entries after ~12:54 (tr_dc4dd324c0ed). emailservice still serves traffic with zero errors (tr_c0d43c9cb03d), so its alert reflects absent upstream work. The sub-millisecond failing durations argue directly against dependency_latency. Note that cartservice is cleared by positive trace evidence, not by its empty metric series (tr_9059d8e2b3e8), which was an instrumentation gap — the retrieved cart incidents are exactly about misreading a flat/absent cart series as health. That leaves bad_deploy, bad_config and resource_exhaustion inside shippingservice with no evidence separating them, since nothing was queried there.
